- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.6) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.2), model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% to reflect risk reversal.
- Model consistently overreacts to short-term spikes (e.g., +5%+ in 1–2 days); cap forecast increase after spike to 2–4% max.
- If 3+ consecutive days of high sentiment + rising prices, model often fails to mean-revert; apply downward correction after 3–5 days of upward momentum.
- Forecast horizon 30d often misses 1–2 week mean reversion; if sentiment shifts from bullish to neutral, reduce forecast slope by 10–20%.
- If true outcome exceeds forecast by >5% for 2+ consecutive days, model is lagging; adjust forecast to match recent 7-day moving average.
- When sentiment history shows alternating bullish/bearish cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
